rationale: The rent/restraint legs are identical to the archived ResearchCommitmentPersistenceHarvest and the gate — a five-year count of material research intensity shifted back two years — overlaps three of five years with the archived gate, so this is a cosmetic re-lagging rather than a substantively different construct.

This fixes a genuine internal inconsistency in the archive's winners (a capex-based restraint leg that mechanically penalizes the very research-intensive firms the gate selects) by using the independently validated capex-net-of-R&D commitment measure, and the signed-contrast form is coherent with the stated two-sided hypothesis.

It imports an economically distinct input channel (labour productivity, whose archived versions showed strong slopes but zero alpha) and applies a specific, well-diagnosed fix — the research-persistence gate — so the test is informative whichever way it comes out, with only annual-emp staleness as a modest concern.

The legs are identical to the archived ResearchAbandonmentWhilePushingCapacity and only the gate is swapped from a single lagged R&D vintage to a lagged persistence count, which is defensible given how much gate construction mattered on the long side but is nonetheless an incremental variant rather than a new mechanism.

The contrast legs are the exact sign-flip of the archived ResearchAbandonmentWhilePushingCapacity with only a gate swap, and it is additionally the near-negative of proposal 4 in this same batch, so it is a rediscovery that adds no independent information.

Substituting total hard-asset commitment (capex plus inventory build over assets) for the capex-over-plant restraint leg does add a real economic channel that was validated on the short side, but it is one of two restraint-leg swaps of the same archived winner in this batch and the weaker-motivated of the two.
